title: Section 9 HMA — Restitution of conjugal rights

content.overview: Section 9 allows either spouse to petition for restitution of conjugal rights when the other has withdrawn from the society of the petitioner without reasonable excuse; the court may decree restitution if satisfied of the truth of the statements and that there is no legal ground why the application should not be granted.
content.study: The petition turns on withdrawal without reasonable excuse; the burden to prove reasonable excuse lies on the withdrawing spouse once withdrawal is shown. Pair with divorce under section 13 (including non-compliance with a restitution decree as a ground) and with interim and permanent maintenance under sections 24 and 25. Constitutional challenges to restitution have been raised but the provision remains on the statute book.

learningObjectives: Explain Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 Section 9 and its statutory purpose.
Identify and apply the provision's ingredients to a factual problem.
Distinguish the provision from related HMA remedies.
enhancement.definition: Section 9 provides a statutory remedy of restitution of conjugal rights where one spouse has withdrawn from the society of the other without reasonable excuse, subject to the court being satisfied that the petition is true and no legal ground bars relief.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: The central issue is withdrawal from the society of the petitioner without reasonable excuse. The provision also requires the court to consider whether any legal ground exists against granting the decree.
enhancement.statutoryFramework: Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, Section 9, read with Section 23 and related matrimonial procedure provisions.
essentialIngredients: A valid marriage governed by the Act.
Withdrawal by one spouse from the society of the other.
Absence of reasonable excuse for the withdrawal.
Court satisfaction as to the truth of the petition and absence of a legal ground against relief.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 9 is a matrimonial remedy concerned with restoration of cohabitation. The factual inquiry is not merely whether spouses live separately; the court must examine whether one spouse has withdrawn from the society of the other and whether there is a reasonable excuse. The Supreme Court has treated conjugal rights as connected with the institution of marriage and has upheld the constitutional validity of Section 9.
examples: If a spouse leaves the matrimonial relationship without a reasonable excuse and the other spouse seeks restoration of cohabitation, the petitioner must establish the withdrawal; the respondent can resist the decree by establishing a reasonable excuse or another legal bar.
enhancement.distinctions: Section 9 seeks restitution of conjugal rights; Section 13 contains divorce grounds, including consequences connected with non-resumption after certain matrimonial decrees; Sections 24 and 25 concern financial relief.

caseLaw.name: Saroj Rani v. Sudarshan Kumar Chadha
caseLaw.holding: The Supreme Court upheld the constitutional validity of Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act and discussed restitution of conjugal rights as a matrimonial remedy.

enhancement.problemApplication: Identify the marriage, withdrawal, evidence of withdrawal, claimed reasonable excuse, and any statutory bar under the Act before determining whether a Section 9 decree can be granted.
